collect.summary:
I worked mainly from the digitised Munich copy of the 1556 book (BSB A.gr.b. 3057, bsb10170656). The HathiTrust copy was blocked by a Cloudflare check, so I could not use it.

1. Title page, imprint, date. The title page reads in full: "Pselli, doctiss. viri, perspicuus liber de quatuor Mathematicis scientijs ... Graecè & Latinè nunc primùm editus. Guilielmo Xylandro Augustano interprete: Cum nonnullis eiusdem Annotationibus. Accessit ... de Philosophia ... Carmen ... Item aliud, De Ioannis Zonarae Annalibus ...: & in ... Xysti Betuleij praeceptoris sui obitum Naenia. Basileae, per Ioannem Oporinum." No year is printed, and the Munich copy has no colophon, errata or index. The date 1556 comes from the dedication.

2. Order of parts.
- Latin part, paginated separately (pp. 1–163; the last page is misnumbered 263):
  - title page;
  - dedication, pp. 3–16;
  - Latin translation, pp. 17–117. Its margins carry topic notes and references to Euclid.
  - "Annotationes quaedam", pp. 118–163. They open with a note "Lectori candido" and continue with an essay on the mathematical sciences, then notes In Arithmeticam, In Musicam, In Geometriam, In Astronomiam.
- Greek part, separate pagination and Greek signatures (pp. 1–175):
  - Greek text, pp. 1–103, with no separate title page or preface;
  - Carmen de philosophia, pp. 104–152;
  - the Zonaras poems, pp. 153–161;
  - the Naenia for Betuleius, pp. 162–175, dated 1554.

3. Dedication. It is addressed to Count Ulrich Fugger and dated "Augustae, ad Nonas Novembres, Anni 1556". It praises patronage and names Hieronymus Wolf as Xylander's helper and as the one who advised the dedication. Xylander says he was the first to put the work into Latin, rendered it "summa fide & perspicuitate", and added notes for beginners. The dedication says nothing about the Greek source, the state of the text or the marginal signs.

4. What the Annotationes say about the text.
- Several Greek readings "perperam/male legebantur":
  - the swapped ἥττονες/μείζονες;
  - πράγμασι for πρίσμασι;
  - δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων / δὶς διὰ πέντε for διὰ πασῶν καὶ ....
- Two conjectures restore the iambic section titles: τῶν before Γεωμετρίας, and "ἄθροισις εὐσύνοπτος ἥδ' ἀστρονομίας".
- One passage is called obscure, and the astronomical passages "depravatus/depravati".
- He dates Psellus by Zonaras to about 1070 AD. He thinks the year numbers in the text are corrupt but changes nothing, "destitutus fide exemplaris".
- He never names his Greek source.

5. Marginal notes in the Greek text. I checked every Greek page by its outer margin (inner margins only on a few pages).
- Outside the music section there are 23 notes:
  - 11 in arithmetic, on pp. 2, 5, 6 (two), 10, 12, 15, 16 (two), 20, 21;
  - 6 in geometry, on pp. 40, 41, 49, 52, 71, 72;
  - 6 in astronomy, on pp. 80, 83, 89, 97, 102, 103.
  - There are also three asterisks in the text with no marginal note, on pp. 50, 54 and 73.
- The system is the same as in music: an asterisk in the text, keyed to an asterisk in the margin giving the corrected Greek, sometimes abbreviated. The Latin wording also matches: "abundat" (p. 71) is like music's "abundant omnino, & delenda sunt"; there are also "Forte ...", "Lege ... uno vocabulo" and "Vide Annotationes".
- The dagger and "addo" appear only in the music section: about 10 notes on pp. 25–32.

6. Editio princeps. It was printed at Venice by Stefano Sabio and brothers, 4 December 1532 (Legrand no. 88), from Arsenios of Monemvasia's text. It was dedicated to Cardinal Niccolò Ridolfi, with a covering letter by Francesco Contarini. In his Greek dedication Arsenios already doubted the author: "εἴτε Ψελλὸς ἦν ὡς τοῖς πλείοσι δοκεῖ, εἴτ' Εὐθύμιος". I found no source naming the manuscript he printed from.
- There is a reprint, Paris: Jacques Bogard, 1545 (BSB digitised). I compared it with Xylander's text and the two agree in the errors Xylander corrects in his margin. Xylander's printed section titles differ only by his own conjectures. This fits his having set his text from the printed edition (1532 or its reprint), but it is my inference; I did not see the 1532 edition itself.

7. Later reprints and judgments before 1900.
- Reprints of the Latin only: Heidelberg, Smesmann, 1591 (VD16 M 5146; arithmetic, music and geometry; without preface and notes according to Fabricius–Harles) and Leiden, Elzevir, 1647 (in the "Compendium mathematicum"; the Annotationes appear to be absent).
- Fabricius–Harles X (1807) lists the editions and repeats Arsenios's doubt. It also takes the year 6516 (= 1008 AD) as Psellus's own date.
- Kästner (1796) says Xylander seems to have printed the Greek faithfully, wrong readings included, and corrected them in the margin.
- Cantor (1894) says the work cannot be wholly by Psellus because the astronomy is dated 1008.
- Schöll (ADB 1898) calls the Psellus compilation worthless.

findings.claim: The full title page of the BSB copy reads: 'PSELLI, doctiss. uiri, perspicuus liber de quatuor Mathematicis scientijs, Arithmetica, Musica, Geometria, & Astronomia: Graecè & Latinè nunc primùm editus. GVILIELMO XYLANDRO Augustano interprete: Cum nonnullis eiusdem Annotationibus. ACCESSIT Eiusdem G. Xylandri de Philosophia, & eius partibus, Carmen longè doctissimum. Item aliud, De IOANNIS ZONARAE Annalibus, eorumq; editione: & in opt. atq; doctiss. uiri XYSTI Betuleij praeceptoris sui obitum Naenia.' The imprint line is covered by a library label but shows through on the verso as 'BASILEAE, PER IOANNEM Oporinum.' No year is printed.
findings.source: Psellus, Perspicuus liber, Basel: Oporinus [1556], BSB A.gr.b. 3057, scan 3 (title) and scan 4 (verso, show-through)

findings.claim: Kästner, describing his own copy, confirms that the printer gives no year and that the date comes from the dedication to Ulrich Fugger, dated 'Augustae ad Nonas Novembres anni 1556'.
findings.source: A. G. Kästner, Geschichte der Mathematik I (Göttingen 1796), p. 279

findings.claim: The BSB copy is a presentation copy with a handwritten dedication on the title page, partly under a library label and legible in mirror image through the leaf: 'Clarissimo viro D[omi]no Jo. Hainrico Herwarto P. Augustano, patrono suo et sum[mo] fautori, Guil. Xylander d.d.' (my reading; the words after 'patrono suo' are uncertain). A librarian wrote 'mit Xylander's Autograph' on the front flyleaf, which also carries the ex-libris 'Ex Electorali Bibliotheca Serenissimorum Utriusque Bavariae Ducum'.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, scans 2-4

findings.claim: The recipient Jo. Hainrich Herwart is presumably the Augsburg patrician Johann Heinrich Herwart (1520-1583), whose library later went to the Bavarian ducal library.
findings.source: general knowledge

findings.claim: BSB catalogues the extent as '263 [i.e. 163], 175 S.'. The last page of the Latin part (end of the Annotationes) is misnumbered 263 for 163.
findings.source: BSB IIIF manifest metadata for bsb10170656; scan 165

findings.claim: Signatures seen in the BSB copy: Latin part a2 (p. 3), b (p. 17), h4 (p. 119), k4 (p. 151); Greek part α (p. 1), ε5 (p. 73), κ5 (p. 153). This fits octavo gatherings of 8: Latin a–k8 plus 2 leaves (pp. 161-164, the last page blank) and Greek α–λ8 (pp. 1-176, the last page blank). The formula is my inference, not a catalogue statement. VD16 (gateway-bayern) was blocked by a bot check.

findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, scans 3-341

findings.claim: Kästner gives the same layout: dedication, Latin translation and notes 264 octavo pages; the Greek 103 pages; Xylander's poem(s) pp. 104-175. He adds that the translation shows contents and Euclid parallels in its margin and has figures, while the Greek has none.
findings.source: Kästner, Geschichte der Mathematik I (1796), pp. 279-280

findings.claim: The BSB copy has no colophon, errata or index. The Greek part ends on p. 175 with the Naenia's closing date line and a blank verso. The Latin part ends on p. '263' [163] with 'FINIS. Deo soli gloria.' and a blank verso. The only end-matter notes are the Annotationes (Latin part pp. 118-163). In the same binding follows a separate work, Martin Borrhaus, In Cosmographiae elementa commentatio (Basel, Oporinus).

The dedication is headed 'Magnifico et generoso, virtutum eruditionisque splendore ornatiss. viro, Dn. Vlricho Fuggero, Kirchbergae, Vueissenhornique Comiti, unico studiorum liberalium patrono, Domino suo, Guilielmus Xylander Augustanus S.' (sig. a2r, p. 3). It ends 'Vale: Augustae, ad Nonas Novembres, Anni 1556. T. Dn. atq; Magnif. studiosissimus Guil. Xylander August.' (p. 16).
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, pp. 3 and 16 (scans 5 and 18)

findings.claim: In the dedication Xylander calls the work 'Pselli hoc utilissimum opusculum, quod de Graeco sermone in Latinum primus converti, illustravique Annotationibus'.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, pp. 6-7 (scans 8-9), dedication
findings.quote: quod de Graeco sermone in Latinum primus converti, illustravique Annotationibus

findings.claim: Xylander says he rendered Psellus into Latin so that those without Greek could read him, 'qua potui summa fide & perspicuitate'. He added notes for beginners ('tironum causa'), which he trusts will shed much light, and says both tasks cost him no small labour.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, pp. 14-15 (scans 16-17)
findings.quote: Latinum qua potui summa fide & perspicuitate reddidi

findings.claim: Xylander says he often heard of Fugger's learning from Hieronymus Wolf, 'meorum conatuum fidelissimo adiutore'. He dedicated the book chiefly on Wolf's advice ('praestantissimi VVolfii consilium'), Wolf having assured him nothing would please Fugger more.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, pp. 9-10 and 12 (scans 11-12, 14)

findings.claim: Xylander describes himself as lacking means since youth and beset by misfortunes ('tot incommodis, infortunijs, miserijs oppugnatus'), comparing his Ate to the one Homer says pursued Hercules from birth. He says he has nonetheless not abandoned his studies.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, pp. 10-11 (scans 12-13)

findings.topic: Dedication: silence on source and text
findings.claim: The dedication (pp. 3-16, read in full) says nothing about the Greek source (printed or manuscript), the state of the Greek text, his corrections or any marginal signs. It does not question Psellus's authorship; it speaks of 'Pselli opusculum' throughout.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, pp. 3-16 (scans 5-18; BSB OCR checked against images)

findings.claim: The Annotationes open with 'Lectori candido S.' Xylander thinks the book worthy of public use with beginners in the schools and hopes professors will expound it. Meanwhile he wants to help those who study without a teacher, as he himself was almost forced to do and still is ('sicut ipse quoque ferè coactus fui facere, & adhuc cogor'). He explains the harder places 'paucis, sed fideliter'.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 118 (scan 120)

findings.topic: Marginal notes (statement in the note to the reader)
findings.claim: The only statement about marginal notes in the prefatory matter concerns the Latin translation: 'In margine quidem ferè, ubi Euclides, princeps in his rebus, eadem tractaret, annotavi'. The Latin margins do carry references such as 'Euclides ab initio 7.' and 'Euclides lib. 9. propos. 32.' He says nothing anywhere about the asterisks in the Greek margins.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 118 (scan 120); pp. 17, 21 (scans 19, 23)

findings.claim: Xylander credits the philosophical introduction ('De Mathematicis scientiis') mostly to his teacher Jacob Schegk of Tübingen ('Eius enim pleraque haec sunt'). Among his hardest blows he counts having had to leave Schegk's instruction in mid-course.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part pp. 125-126 (scans 127-128)

findings.topic: State of the Greek text: corrections (arithmetic)
findings.claim: On deficient and abundant numbers: 'Diminuti sunt.) In Graeco hae definitiones perperam legebantur, his vocib. ἥττονες & μείζονες inuersè una pro alia scriptis: quod ipsa etiam Pselli exempla docent.'
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 134 (scan 136)
findings.quote: In Graeco hae definitiones perperam legebantur

findings.topic: State of the Greek text: corrections (arithmetic)
findings.claim: 'Diapason cum diatess.) In Graeco malè legebatur δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων, & δὶς διὰ πέντε, pro διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων, & διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ πέντε: ut deinde in musica demonstrabo.' This is an arithmetic note that looks ahead to the music section.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 136 (scan 138)

findings.topic: State of the Greek text: corrections (arithmetic)
findings.claim: 'Serratilib.) Malè in graeco legebatur πράγμασι pro πρίσμασι, luculento errore.'
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 143 (scan 145)
findings.quote: Malè in graeco legebatur πράγμασι pro πρίσμασι

findings.claim: On the Greek πρόλογοι / ὑπόλογοι Xylander explains that he avoided rendering them as 'dux / comes', since those words are used mostly of single numbers, so as not to obscure the author's sense.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 134 (scan 136)

findings.claim: In Geometriam: 'Graeca iambica inscriptio videtur articulum τῶν desiderare, ante vocabulum Γεωμετρίας, ut versus stet.' In Astronomiam: 'Iambus inscriptionis hic quoque non constat. Puto legendum, ἄθροισις εὐσύνοπτος ἥδ' ἀστρονομίας.' My reading of the second word comes from a ligature; it matches the printed Greek heading on p. 76.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part pp. 151 and 161 (scans 153, 163)

findings.topic: Conjectures put into the printed Greek
findings.claim: Xylander's printed Greek headings carry his metrical conjectures: p. 34 'ΣΥΝΟΨΙΣ ΑΥΤΗ ΤΩΝ ΓΕΩΜΕΤΡΙΑΣ λόγων'; p. 76 'ΑΘΡΟΙΣΙΣ ΕΥΣΥΝΟΠΤΟΣ ΗΔ' ΑΣΤΡΟΝΟΜΙΑΣ'. The Paris 1545 reprint of the 1532 text has 'ΣΥΝΟΨΙΣ ΑΥΤΗ, ΓΕΩΜΕΤΡΙΑΣ λόγων' (f. 27v) and 'ΑΘΡΟΙΣΙΣ ΕΥΣΥΝΟΠΤΟΣ, ἀστρονομίας' (f. 57v), without τῶν and ἥδ'. So he printed the conjectures in the text and justified them only in the Annotationes.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek pp. 34, 76 (scans 200, 242); Paris 1545 (BSB bsb10169572), scans 54, 114

findings.topic: State of the text: obscure and corrupt places
findings.claim: On the closing verses of the geometry: 'Locus est obscurus, perplexus, et sic satis ambiguus, ut diuinandum ferè fuerit de sensu.' On the astronomy: 'Finitor dum circumagitur.) Non video, quomodo hic locus non sit depravatus' (polar circles are drawn from the poles of the zodiac, not from the horizon). On the year numbers: 'Hi numeri annorum hic, & deinde, depravati sunt proculdubio.'
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part pp. 161-162 (scans 163-164)

findings.claim: Xylander adds that Psellus lived under Romanus Diogenes, was a senator of great authority, and taught Michael (son of Constantine Ducas), citing 'Ioan. Zonaras Monachus in suis Chronicis'. Hence Psellus flourished 'circa annum mundi 5030, post natum Christum annis circiter 1070'. He finds the text's year count 'mihi certè vehementer suspectus' but alters nothing: 'Nihil tam[en] habeo quòd mutem, destitutus fide exemplaris.' He does not doubt Psellus's authorship.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 162 (scan 164)
findings.quote: Nihil tam habeo quòd mutem, destitutus fide exemplaris.

findings.claim: In the general part of the Annotationes Xylander treats Psellus as the author without hesitation, e.g. 'Talis enim scientia est Musica, qualem Psellus, Boethius, & alij tradiderunt'.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 124 [printed '134'] (scan 126)

findings.claim: The Annotationes end by asking readers to take his labour in good part. If he learns it was welcome, he promises fuller and more accurate notes soon for beginners: 'non enim haec doctoribus, aut artificib. scribimus: quin & ipsi inter discipulos etiamnum uelle nos haberi, liberè prae nobis ferimus'.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part pp. 162-163 (scans 164-165)

findings.claim: In the geometry notes Xylander refers readers to his German commentaries on Euclid ('in meis vulgari lingua scriptis Commentarijs, ad secundi libri Elementorum Euclidis principium'; also notes on book I prop. 35 and books II and IV). Kästner and Schöll both observe that this German Euclid was printed only in 1562, six years later.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Latin part p. 151 (scan 153); Kästner I (1796) p. 281; Schöll, ADB 44 (1898) pp. 582-593

findings.topic: Marginal notes in the Greek text: arithmetic
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek pp. 1-22 (scans 167-188), outer margins of every page checked on images

findings.topic: Marginal notes in the Greek text: geometry
findings.claim: Greek geometry (pp. 34-75) has 6 marginal notes: p. 40 '*προσεκ.'; p. 41 '*προσεκ.'; p. 49 '*ἅτε.'; p. 52 '*Forte ἐπιπέμπτου.'; p. 71 '*abundat'; p. 72 '*δε(?)'. Three asterisks in the text have no marginal note anywhere visible on the page: p. 50 ('ὁ * κατὰ διάμετρον'), p. 54 ('αὐτοῖς * παραλληλεπιπέδοις'), p. 73 ('ἀρχιμήδης*').
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek pp. 34-75 (scans 200-241)

findings.topic: Marginal notes in the Greek text: astronomy
findings.claim: Greek astronomy (pp. 76-103) has 6 marginal notes: p. 80 '*ὑποπ.'; p. 83 '*εἰκοστῆς'; p. 89 '*ὁμοταχῶς'; p. 97 '*ἀσυμ.'; p. 102 '*ἢ καὶ τὸν ἄρατ.(?)'; p. 103 '*τῇ(?)'.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek pp. 76-103 (scans 242-269)

findings.claim: The Greek music section (pp. 23-33) has about 10 notes on pp. 25, 28, 29, 31, 32. They use both asterisk and dagger (†) and Latin formulas: '... addo', '†iterum eadem verba addo' (p. 25), '*abundant omnino, & delenda sunt' (p. 29).
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek pp. 23-33 (scans 189-199), margins only

findings.claim: The other three sections use the same system as music: an asterisk in the text keyed to an asterisk in the margin with the proposed Greek word, often abbreviated. Their Latin formulas are of the same kind: 'abundat' (geometry p. 71, like music's 'abundant ... delenda sunt'), 'Forte ...' (pp. 10, 52), 'Lege ... uno vocabulo' (p. 16), 'Vide Annotationes' (p. 12). But the dagger and 'addo' occur only in the music section. Count outside music: 23 notes (11 + 6 + 6), against about 10 in the 11 music pages, so music is much denser.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek pp. 1-103 (scans 167-269), outer margins checked page by page on IIIF crops

findings.claim:
Legrand describes the editio princeps (no. 88) as follows.
Greek title: 'Τοῦ σοφωτάτου Ψελλοῦ, σύνταγμα εὐσύνοπτον εἰς τὰς τέσσαρας μαθηματικὰς ἐπιστήμας ...'.
Latin title: 'Sapientissimi Pselli opus dilucidum in quattuor Mathematicas disciplinas ...'.
Imprint: 'Venetiis. MDXXXII. Cum gratia'.
Colophon: 'Ἐνετίῃσι παρὰ Στεφάνῳ Σαβίῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ ... ποσειδεῶνος τετάρτῃ' (dated 4 December 1532).
Format: petit in-8°, 56 unnumbered leaves in 14 gatherings of 4.
Legrand calls it 'Édition princeps, d'une excessive rareté'. Copy: BnF V 1960 Réserve.
findings.source: É. Legrand, Bibliographie hellénique ... XVe et XVIe siècles, vol. I (Paris 1885), pp. 212-215, no. 88

findings.claim: The 1532 edition has two prefatory pieces. On the verso of f. 1 is a Latin letter 'Nicolao Redulpho Cardinali amplissimo Franciscus Contarenus', saying Psellus's mathematical books were 'typis excussi ab Arsenio, Epidauri archiepiscopo' and asking the cardinal to protect the aged and sick Arsenios. On ff. 2-5 is Arsenios of Monemvasia's Greek dedicatory letter to Cardinal Ridolfi.
findings.source: Legrand, Bibliographie hellénique I (1885), pp. 212-213; reprinted in Paris 1545, scans 2-8

findings.claim: In his dedication Arsenios presents the book as his 'daughter' named Mathematike. He gives it in favour 'to her father, whether he was Psellus, as most think, or Euthymios': 'καὶ ταῦτα τῷ ταύτης πατρί, εἴτε Ψελλὸς ἦν, ὡς τοῖς πλείοσι δοκεῖ, εἴτ' Εὐθύμιος, χαριζόμενος'. Xylander never mentions this doubt.
findings.source: Paris 1545 reprint, f. 3v (BSB bsb10169572, scan 6); same text in Legrand I (1885), p. 214
findings.quote: εἴτε Ψελλὸς ἦν, ὡς τοῖς πλείοσι δοκεῖ, εἴτ' Εὐθύμιος

findings.claim: Neither Arsenios's dedication (read in the 1545 reprint and in Legrand's transcription) nor Legrand's description names the manuscript the 1532 text was printed from.
findings.source: Legrand I (1885), pp. 212-215; Paris 1545, ff. 2r-4v (scans 3-8)

findings.claim: In the dedication of the Venice 1532 Psellus logic (Introductio in sex philosophiae modos, with Jacopo Foscarini's Latin, Sabio, Nov. 1532), Arsenios says he had recently printed and sent Psellus's Mathematica to Ridolfi: 'Ἔναγχος τὰ τοῦ Ψελλοῦ Μαθηματικὰ ἐντυπώσαντες, ἐκπεπόμφαμεν ...'.
findings.source: Legrand I (1885), pp. 209-211

findings.claim: A Greek-only reprint: 'Τοῦ σοφωτάτου Ψελλοῦ, σύνταγμα εὐσύνοπτον ... Doctissimi Pselli opus dilucidum in quattuor Mathematicas disciplinas ... Parisiis, Excudebat Iacobus Bogardus, 1545', 75 leaves in the BSB copy. It reproduces Contarini's Latin letter and Arsenios's Greek dedication. Eton's catalogue gives 76 leaves, 8vo.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 298#Beibd.1 (bsb10169572), scans 1-8; Eton College Library B11614

findings.topic: Relation of Xylander's Greek to the printed tradition
findings.source: Paris 1545 (bsb10169572) scans 10, 16, 37 vs BSB A.gr.b. 3057 Greek pp. 2, 6, 21 (scans 168, 172, 187)

findings.topic: Later judgment: Kästner on Xylander's Greek
findings.claim: Kästner judges that Xylander seems to have printed the Greek faithfully, obviously wrong readings included, and corrected them in the margin. He complains that the four books are not subdivided, so passages are hard to match between Greek and translation.
findings.source: Kästner, Geschichte der Mathematik I (Göttingen 1796), p. 280
findings.quote: Das Griechische hat Xylander, wie es scheint, getreu abdrucken lassen, auch offenbar unrichtige Lesarten, die er am Rande verbessert.

findings.topic: Later judgment: Kästner on the notes
findings.claim: Kästner summarises the Annotationes (Schegk as source of the introduction, the unit and Logistica, the sieve, the reference to the German Euclid). He checks Xylander's numerical test of Psellus's circle rule by logarithms and finds it correct (≈2217.49 for diameter 56).
findings.source: Kästner I (1796), pp. 280-282

findings.claim:
Fabricius-Harles lists the work under Psellus.
- Note h: 'Psellus testatur, se scripsisse anno Graecorum 6516. h. e. Chr. 1008', taken as Psellus's own date.
- Editions listed: Basel, Oporinus 1556 'cum nonnullis eiusdem Xylandri adnotationibus tam criticis, quam exegeticis'; Arsenios's first Greek edition (wrongly placed 'Romae'), noting his Psellus-or-Euthymios doubt; Paris 1545 (Bogard); Vinet's Latin (Paris 1557, Tournon 1592/1591).
- Fabricius also claims 'Post Vinetum Xylander suam interpretationem adgressus est'.
findings.source: J. A. Fabricius, Bibliotheca Graeca, ed. G. C. Harles, vol. X (Hamburg 1807), pp. 46-47 (Lib. V c. XXVIII, no. XXXVII and note h)
Fabricius-Harles, Bibliotheca Graeca X (1807), p. 47 and note i

findings.claim: 'Micaelis Pselli Arithmeticae, Musicae et Geometriae Compendia', Heidelberg: Smesmann, 1591, 59 [1] pp., [2] leaves, Latin, with Xylander as contributor; VD16 M 5146; BSB A.gr.b. 3067. I read only the record, not the book.
findings.source: Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek record (BSB)

findings.claim: 'Michaelis Pselli Compendium mathematicum, aliaque tractatus eodem pertinentes', Lugd. Bat., Ex Officina Elzeviriorum, 1647. The preface 'Ad lectorem' says the tracts were added to a reprint of Sacrobosco's Elementa for school use. The Psellus is headed 'Michaelis Pselli Quadrivium, hoc est, Perspicuus liber de quatuor Mathematicis scientiis ... Gulielmo Xylandro interprete' and reprints the Latin only. The OCR text contains no 'Annotationes', so the notes appear to be absent; I checked only the front matter and searched the OCR.
findings.source: Psellus, Compendium mathematicum (Leiden 1647), archive.org bub_gb_t2AANntDQwUC, front matter

findings.claim: Cantor writes that the work printed under Psellus's name in the 16th century cannot be wholly his, since the astronomy dates itself to 1008, when Psellus was at most an infant. He calls its arithmetic devoid of 'den Schatten eines eigenen Gedankens'. He cites Kästner I, 281-282.
findings.source: M. Cantor, Vorlesungen über Geschichte der Mathematik I, 2nd ed. (Leipzig 1894), pp. 472-473
findings.quote: rührt keinenfalls im Ganzen von ihm her, da die Astronomie sich selbst vom Jahre 1008 datirt

findings.claim: Schöll's ADB article judges the text, not the edition. He writes that Xylander thought 'die werthlose Compilation des Michael Psellus' worth explaining to beginners 'auf Schulen'. He notes that the Naenia for Betuleius, written right after the teacher's death, was printed two years later in the appendix to the Psellus.
findings.source: F. Schöll, 'Xylander, Wilhelm Holtzman', Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie 44 (1898), pp. 582-593
findings.quote: Die werthlose Compilation des Michael Psellus hielt X. für werth

findings.claim: The Naenia is headed 'In obitum piissimi iuxta, doctissimique P. M. viri M. Xysti Betuleij, Augustanae scholae moderatoris ... Guilielmi Xylandri Augustani Naenia. αὐτοσχεδιασθέντα', with the marginal date 'Obijt 13. Kal. Iulij, Anni, &c. 1554. Augustae'. It ends 'Exarata Augustae Vindelicae, Anno, &c. 1554. ad Nonas Iulij'.
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek part pp. 162 and 175 (scans 328, 341)

findings.claim: On p. 153: 'De Ioannis Zonarae Annalibus, eorumque expectatissima editione, Carmen Guilielmi Xylandri Augustani', a Greek elegiac poem beginning 'Ζωναρᾶ ἀγχινόου ...'. A Latin poem 'Eiusdem' follows (p. 157ff.).
findings.source: BSB A.gr.b. 3057, Greek part pp. 153-161 (scans 319-327; BSB OCR)

findings.claim: Arsenios (Aristoboulos) Apostolis, archbishop of Monemvasia, a Cretan collaborator of Aldus, died around 1535.
findings.source: Wikipedia, 'Arsenius Apostolius' (search snippet only); general knowledge

collect.open_questions:
1. Source of Xylander's Greek. In every place I checked, his text agrees with the errors of the Paris 1545 reprint, which he corrects in the margin. Whether he used 1532 or 1545 needs a collation against the Venice 1532 itself (BnF Rés. V 1960; not digitised as far as I found).

2. Manuscript behind the 1532 edition. Not identified; Legrand and Arsenios's dedication are both silent. Moore's Iter Psellianum might help.

3. Unmatched asterisks. Three asterisks in the Greek text (pp. 50, 54, 73) have no marginal note in the Munich copy. A second copy (HathiTrust, blocked) is needed to see whether notes were dropped or never set.

4. Uncertain readings of some marginal notes: p. 15 '*ἑκάστην(?)'; p. 72 '*δε(?)'; p. 102 '*ἢ καὶ τὸν ἄρατ.(?)'; p. 103 '*τῇ(?)'; pp. 40-41 '*προσεκ.' (abbreviation not expanded); p. 16 '*προσθήκη' (margin and text look alike at the resolution I used). Inner (gutter) margins were checked only on a few pages.

5. Quire formula. 'Latin a-k8 + 2 leaves; Greek α-λ8' is my inference from the signatures I saw; VD16 could not be reached to confirm it.

6. Music annotations not read. Xylander's notes 'In Musicam' (Latin part pp. 144 to about 150, BSB scans 146-152) quote lemmata of his Latin music translation, so I did not read them. The user should decide whether they fall under the ban.
- My OCR overview script did show me the first line or so of each of those pages (about 90 characters). I deleted those OCR files.
- I also deleted my downloaded full text of the Leiden 1647 reprint, which contains the Latin music section; I had read only its front matter.
- The shared folder raw/work also contains files and subfolders I did not create (e.g. 'psellus1556', 'vd16_m5144.html'). I did not open them.

7. Unverified editions in Fabricius-Harles: the Wittenberg 1560, Leipzig 1590, 'Augsburg 1554' and Leipzig 1601 'Geometria' editions. Also Fabricius's claim that Vinet's Latin (made 1553) came before Xylander's, against Xylander's 'primus converti'.

8. Pre-1900 judgments of the edition itself. Beyond Kästner (1796) I found none that judge Xylander's text or translation (Allatius, De Psellis, not checked). No pre-1900 source I found says outright that Xylander's Greek derives from 1532.

9. 'Nunc primum editus'. Why the title says this although the Greek had been printed in 1532 and 1545 (most likely it refers to the Greek and Latin together) is not settled by any statement of Xylander's.

Arsenios has two 'daughters' of his own, the Ionia and the ascetic Leimonarion, and an adopted one (ἐπίκτητον), Mathematike. He chose to bring the adopted one out before his own ('προεκθέσθαι ταύτην ἐκείναιν'), 'καὶ ταῦτα τῷ ταύτης πατρί … χαριζόμενος': as a favour to her father, whether Psellus or Euthymios. verify.summary:
I checked all 52 findings, with the scans opened and read, not just the catalogue entries. Downloads are in raw/work (local, not in git)/verify1556.

Result: 43 confirmed, 9 corrected, none wrong or unopenable. The two from-memory findings are now checked: 3 confirmed, 51 corrected.

The corrections:
- **1:** Kästner p. 279 does not say he describes his own copy.
- **30:** On p. 73 the mark after 'ἀρχιμήδης' is a raised point, not an asterisk. Only pp. 50 and 54 have an asterisk in the text with no marginal note.
- **35:** Legrand puts Arsenios's letter in the 1532 edition on ff. 2-3, not ff. 2-5.
- **36:** The Greek quotation is exact, but the paraphrase needs sharpening. Arsenios brings out his adopted 'daughter' Mathematike before his own two works, as a favour to her father (Psellus or Euthymios).
- **44:** Harles cites Pinelli for Venice 1532 (Sabio), not Paris 1532.
- **49:** The Naenia heading reads 'αὐτοσχεδιασθεῖσα'.
- **51:** The date of Arsenios's death is disputed: BnF gives 30 April 1535 in Venice, English Wikipedia gives 1538.

Precision notes on confirmed findings:
- **12:** Wolf's remark was that nothing would please Fugger more than a chance to show his virtues as a patron.
- **21:** Dux/comes are terms for the numbers, not the ratios.
- **33:** Some notes are not keyed with an asterisk (pp. 2, 10, 12, 16).
- **38:** Legrand calls the Greek logic edition undated; the Nov. 1532 colophon belongs to Foscarini's separate Latin plaquette.
- **47:** Cantor's Kästner citation belongs to the circle passage; the 1008 point cites Tannery.

New evidence turned up during the checks:
- A second BSB copy (A.gr.b. 3059) shows the same undated imprint without a label over it.
- Schöll (ADB) names Joh. Heinr. Herward as Xylander's patron and the dedicatee of his Dio Cassius.
- NDB 8 confirms Hans Heinrich Herwart's dates as 1520-83.
- A BSB catalogue of c. 1586/87 records the Herwart collection passing into the Munich court library.
- My own count of the music-section margins also gives exactly 10 notes.

What I did not read, as instructed:
- no translation of the music section, and not Heiberg;
- no Annotationes on music (scans 146-152), which I only searched by machine;
- the 1591 Heidelberg book, of which I read only the catalogue record;
- the music part of the Leiden 1647 Psellus.
